 - Meteorological Overview:

This afternoon there will be an upper-level ridge over North-
central, Central, and Southwestern Montana. This will keep warm 
(well-above seasonal average) temperatures and mostly dry weather 
for the area on Sunday. Due to strong low-level winds it will be 
breezy across North-central, Central, and Southwestern Montana. The 
strongest winds will be in the Madison River Valley and along the 
Rocky Mountain Front. On Monday the upper-level ridge remains over 
North-central, Central, and Southwestern Montana with strong 
southerly flow aloft. On Monday it will remain warm (well-above 
seasonal averages) and mostly dry. 

Monday evening into Tuesday an upper-level trough associated with a 
Pacific cold front will move over North-central, Central, and 
Southwestern Montana. This will bring cooler temperatures and 
widespread precipitation to the area on Tuesday. On Tuesday a 
frontogenetic band of precipitation will move through North-central, 
Central, and Southwestern Montana. This band will cause there to be 
a brief period of heavy precipitation across the area as it moves 
from west to east. Across lower-elevations of North-central and 
Central Montana when this band moves through it has the potential to 
bring a rapid change in precipitation type from rain to snow. See 
the Forecast Confidence & Scenarios Section for details. 

On Wednesday the upper-level trough will remain over North-central, 
Central, and Southwestern Montana. This will allow cold (well-below 
seasonal averages) temperatures to linger across the area. On 
Wednesday morning snow will gradually diminish in a west to east 
fashion across North-central, Central, and Southwestern Montana. On 
Thursday an upper-level ridge briefly moves over North-central, 
Central, and Southwestern Montana. This will allow it to be cool and 
dry across the area on Thursday. Friday through Saturday an upper-
level trough moves over North-central, Central, and Southwestern 
Montana. This will bring another round of precipitation with cold 
temperatures remaining across the area. -IG

 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

From Monday night through Wednesday morning there is high-confidence 
in cold air moving into North-central, Central, and Southwestern 
Montana. There is low-confidence in how fast snow-levels lower on 
Tuesday. However at most mountain locations precipitation will be
all snow. When the cold front passes Monday night there will be a
frontogenetical band of heavy snow along the continental divide. 
During most of the daylight hours across most mountain locations 
most snowfall will melt. Tuesday afternoon/early evening the 
frontogenetical band of precipitation will move eastward. This 
will rapidly turn rain into snow at lower-elevations. There 
remains uncertainty in how fast snow-levels and temperatures drop 
at lower-elevations. However due NBM-warm bias from the previous 
days, hourly temperatures were decreased Tuesday evening through 
Wednesday morning to account for diabatic cooling due to the 
frontogenetic band moving through North-central, Central, and 
Southwestern Montana.

From Monday night through Wednesday morning there is a 30 - 60% 
chance for 6 inches of snow or greater in the Madison and Gallatin 
Mountains, Northwestern Beaverhead County, and along the Southern 
Rocky Mountain Front. From Monday night through Wednesday morning 
there is a 40 - 80% chance for 4 inches of snow or greater across 
the Mountains of North-central, Central, and Southwestern Montana. 
As a result a Winter Weather Advisory was issued for Northwest 
Beaverhead County from 11 PM Monday through 11 PM Tuesday. Between 
Belt and Lewistown along Montana Highway 200/US Highway 87 there is 
a 40 - 60% chance 1 inch of snow or greater from Monday night 
through Wednesday morning. However, that probability is too low 
due to NBM not handling this event very well. Most lower-elevation
locations of North-central, Central, and Southwestern Montana have
at least a 50% chance for receiving 1 inch of snowfall or greater
on grassy surfaces Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday morning. 
Across Central and Southwestern Montana and North-central Montana
along and west of I-15 there is a 40 - 70% chance for one half 
inch of total liquid precipitation Monday night through Wednesday 
morning. -IG
